not_rules.quote: Associate the help text with the label for screen reader users.

not_rules.note: Concerns prepopulation and control defaults, not wording.
not_rules.quote: Use prefilled information and default options if appropriate for the user

not_rules.note: Concerns system population of input values.
not_rules.quote: If it’s appropriate and secure, prefill information.

not_rules.note: G-5: user-research activity.
not_rules.quote: Research with users to make sure they’re comfortable with prefilling.

not_rules.note: Concerns page arrangement; the request to check and correct the information is a separate text requirement.
not_rules.quote: Present prefilled information on its own page.

not_rules.note: Concerns selected control states, not option wording.
not_rules.quote: Never include pre-selected gender or sex options.

not_rules.note: Concerns validation functionality; error-message wording is marked separately.
not_rules.quote: Add validation to help the user to complete digital forms

not_rules.note: Introduces functional checks on entered data, not requirements for the form's prose.
not_rules.quote: Apply verification checks for:

not_rules.note: Concerns visual validation feedback.
not_rules.quote: You can help some users complete the form by adding colour to show if an input is valid.

not_rules.note: Concerns visual and programmatic accessibility of validation status.
not_rules.quote: Don’t use colour alone, and make sure assistive technology can detect validation.

not_rules.note: Concerns the interface treatment of ineligibility. The required explanatory content is marked separately.
not_rules.quote: If the user is not eligible for a service, don’t show a validation error.

not_rules.note: G-5: reference back to validation guidance, not another text requirement.
not_rules.quote: Follow the guidance to add validation to help the user to complete the digital forms.

not_rules.note: Concerns save-and-resume functionality.
not_rules.quote: Help the user save and resume complex digital forms

not_rules.note: Requires a functional control.
not_rules.quote: Include a button for the user to save a draft as they work through complex forms.

not_rules.note: Concerns application state and navigation.
not_rules.quote: The form should reopen to the page they were on.

not_rules.note: Concerns generation and display of a transaction identifier, not its wording.
not_rules.quote: Display a receipt code when the user submits the form.

not_rules.note: Introduces visual branding guidance.
not_rules.quote: Add only essential branding

not_rules.note: G-5: consultation instruction.
not_rules.quote: Talk to your communications team for guidelines on how to brand forms.

not_rules.note: Concerns external branding and presentation requirements rather than a specific wording rule.
not_rules.quote: Make sure print and digital forms meet the Australian Government branding guidelines.

not_rules.note: Concerns non-textual visual elements.
not_rules.quote: Only include icons, images or colour when research shows they help the user understand the form.

not_rules.note: Concerns image accessibility, not form wording.
not_rules.quote: Make sure you create accessible images.

rules.quote: Organise content in the form using section headings.
rules.violation_condition: A form groups questions into sections but provides no section headings.
when: Applies when questions are grouped into sections.
rules.why: G-1: the grouping heading is a section; this body sentence states a specific content requirement.

rules.quote: Describe the topic or the following section in the headings.
rules.violation_condition: A form section heading does not describe the topic or content of the section it introduces.
when: Applies to form section headings.
rules.why: The rule-grain test separates a missing heading from an existing heading that misdescribes its section.

covers.quote: Try to use one word or a short phrase as a label.
Include one short label for every form question to make it clear to the user what to do.

rules.quote: Write short active content for forms, including ‘help text’ and error messages – this is called ‘microcopy’.
rules.specification: This check concerns brevity, not grammatical voice. Interpret 'short' as avoiding unnecessary wording; the page provides no numerical length limit. Button labels should normally be one word or a short action phrase.
rules.violation_condition: Form content is unnecessarily long or wordy for its immediate purpose.
when: Includes questions, labels, help text and error messages.
rules.why: The rule-grain test separates brevity from active voice; G-2 consolidates the special cases for short labels.

rules.quote: Write short active content for forms, including ‘help text’ and error messages – this is called ‘microcopy’.
rules.violation_condition: Form content uses a passive construction rather than active wording.
when: Includes help text and error messages.
rules.why: The rule-grain test separates grammatical voice from the independent requirement for brevity.

covers.quote: Write and design forms starting with plain language. Include the terms that are familiar to users.
If they help the user understand and use the form, keep them.

rules.quote: Use familiar words in familiar ways
rules.specification: Assess familiarity against the intended users and the terms they use for the topic. The page supplies no fixed vocabulary list.
rules.violation_condition: A form uses unfamiliar or unexpected terminology, or uses familiar words in a way its intended users would not recognise.
when: Retain terms that testing shows help users understand and use the form.
Terms that some users do not understand need plain language definitions.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the heading and its restatements; G-2 records the testing condition without making testing a text rule.

rules.quote: If some users don’t understand the terms, include plain language definitions.
rules.violation_condition: A form contains terms that some intended users do not understand but supplies no plain language definitions.
when: Applies when some intended users do not understand a term used in the form.
rules.why: The rule-grain test distinguishes an omitted definition from the choice of unfamiliar terminology.

covers.quote: Before a user starts a form, they need to know:
what the form is for and if they need to fill it in
who can use the form (if they are eligible for the service)
what they need to submit the form (for example, tax file number and passport number)
if they can ask someone else to fill it in for them
what happens after they submit it and any other stages.
If the form is part of a service that will involve other stages, show the full service process with a task list. Include information about any other forms the user will need to fill in.

rules.quote: Say who the form is for and what they need
rules.violation_condition: The information available before a user starts a form omits its purpose, eligibility, submission requirements, whether someone else can complete it, or what happens after submission.
when: Provide this information before the user starts the form.
For a service with other stages, show the full service process in a task list and include other forms the user will need to complete.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the required pre-start information and the multistage-service case in one disclosure rule.

covers.quote: You don’t need to mark questions as ‘required’ because you will only be asking for information that is needed.

rules.quote: Don’t mark ‘required’ questions
rules.violation_condition: A form marks questions as required.
when: The guidance assumes the form asks only for information that is needed.
Questions inviting voluntary additional information should instead be marked optional.
rules.why: G-4 uses the instructive heading rather than promoting its permissive explanation into another rule.

covers.quote: Collect the least amount needed for the function or activity related to the form.
only ask for what you need

rules.quote: You must only collect personal information if it is necessary.
rules.violation_condition: A form requests personal information that is unnecessary for its function or activity, or requests more personal detail than that function or activity needs.
when: Applies to personal information requested by the form.
Assess necessity against the function or activity related to the form.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates necessity and minimum collection as one personal-information minimisation check.

covers.quote: Use a collection statement on the form.

rules.quote: Tell people when and why you are collecting their personal information, and what their privacy rights are.
rules.violation_condition: A form collecting personal information lacks a collection statement explaining when and why it is collected and the person's privacy rights.
when: Applies when the form collects personal information.
The collection statement must be on the form.
rules.why: G-4 treats the collection statement as the implementation of the disclosure requirement, not a second rule.

covers.quote: Sometimes you need to invite the user to tell you something they think is important and they want us to know (for example, to collect feedback).

rules.quote: Mark these questions as ‘optional’.
rules.violation_condition: A question inviting voluntary additional information is not marked optional.
when: Applies to invitations for users to provide something they consider important and want the organisation to know, such as feedback.
rules.why: G-2 records the condition in the preceding sentence; the marking requirement is independently actionable.

covers.quote: For forms that have more than one question, number the questions.

rules.quote: Number the questions
rules.violation_condition: A form containing more than one question leaves its questions unnumbered.
when: Applies to forms with more than one question.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the heading and body; G-2 preserves the explicit question-count condition.

rules.quote: Only include a question if it is relevant to the user.
rules.violation_condition: A form presents a question that does not apply to the user or their circumstances.
when: Assess relevance for the user or route through the form.
rules.why: This sentence constrains question content, unlike the preceding instruction about disabling input controls.

covers.quote: Make sure the button action matches what it says it does.

rules.quote: The label must clearly describe what happens when the user selects the button.
rules.violation_condition: A form button's label does not clearly describe the action or result of selecting it, or promises an action different from the one performed.
when: Applies to labels on form action buttons, including secondary buttons.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the secondary-button restatement; the requirement concerns label meaning rather than button design.

covers.quote: Include one short label for every form question to make it clear to the user what to do.
Write clear labels and ‘help text’ instead of placeholder text.

rules.quote: Write labels for every question
rules.violation_condition: A form question has no label identifying what the user should do, or has competing labels rather than one question label.
when: Applies to every form question.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the heading and body; label brevity and prohibited placeholder text are handled by their own checks.

rules.quote: Write labels without a colon at the end.
rules.violation_condition: A form question label ends with a colon.
when: Applies to form question labels.
rules.why: The rule-grain test separates this specific punctuation check from the requirement to supply a label.

covers.quote: Write clear labels and ‘help text’ instead of placeholder text.

rules.quote: Don’t put anything in the field the user will type in – this is called ‘placeholder text’.
rules.violation_condition: A digital form input contains placeholder text for the user to read before entering an answer.
when: Applies to placeholder text, not actual prefilled user information.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the prohibition and its alternative; the later permission for prefilling distinguishes actual answers from placeholders.

rules.quote: If you have one question per page, use that question as the heading for the page.
rules.violation_condition: A digital form page with one question uses a different page heading instead of the question.
when: Applies to digital form pages containing one question.
rules.why: The body states a text-equivalence requirement; the surrounding HTML-element instructions are not text rules.

covers.quote: Write extra text to help the user complete the question the first time they try.
In very complex forms, you might need to link to more detailed explanation.
Write clear labels and ‘help text’ instead of placeholder text.

rules.quote: Include ‘help text’ to provide more context
rules.specification: Interpret help text as required where the question or label alone does not provide enough context to answer correctly, not as mandatory extra text for every self-explanatory question.
rules.violation_condition: A form question lacks the additional explanation a user needs to answer it correctly on the first attempt.
when: Very complex forms may link to a more detailed explanation.
rules.why: G-4 consolidates the heading and body; G-3 records the optional link as a case rather than a separate rule.

rules.quote: Don’t use headings, labels or placeholder text for help text.
rules.specification: Check help text misused as headings or labels here. Cite the blanket placeholder-text rule for help placed in input placeholders, avoiding a second finding for the same placeholder.
rules.violation_condition: Supplementary instructions explaining how to answer a question are presented as a heading or question label instead of separate help text.
when: Applies to explanatory help text.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the alternative misuses together; the rule-grain test avoids duplicating the blanket placeholder prohibition.

covers.quote: If users are not asked to confirm details they might miss them.

rules.quote: Ask the user to check and correct the information as part of the form page.
rules.violation_condition: A form presents prefilled information without asking the user to check it and correct any errors.
when: Applies when the form presents prefilled information.
The request belongs on the form page presenting that information.
rules.why: The rule-grain test separates the required instruction to the user from the non-textual decision to prefill fields.

rules.quote: Write error messages so they help the user act on the problem.
rules.violation_condition: A digital form error message does not explain the problem in a way that helps the user take corrective action.
when: Applies to digital form error messages.
rules.why: The rule-grain test separates actionable guidance from the independent prohibition on blaming the user.

rules.quote: Do not blame them for making a mistake.
rules.violation_condition: A form error message blames or reproaches the user for an input mistake.
when: Applies to digital form error messages.
rules.why: The rule-grain test treats blaming language as a distinct finding from missing corrective guidance.

covers.quote: why they can’t use the service
their options.

rules.quote: Use a separate page that explains:
rules.violation_condition: The explanation given to an ineligible user omits why they cannot use the service or what their options are.
when: Applies when a user is not eligible for a service.
The explanation is provided on a separate page rather than as a validation error.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the two required parts of the ineligibility explanation in one content requirement.
